description: Claim-support cases for the Northwind Labs synthetic knowledge base. Each claim is labeled against the documents. Four labels exercise the failure modes a citation-grounded checker must handle: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, NOT_IN_DOCS (plausible but absent - the case naive RAG fails by hallucinating support), and PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (one part holds, another does not).

cases.claim: New hires accrue 18 PTO days per year.
cases.label: SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: HR-001 2.1 states new employees accrue 18 days per calendar year.

cases.claim: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all company systems.
cases.label: SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: SEC-001 1.2 makes MFA mandatory for all company systems.

cases.claim: Application logs are retained for 90 days.
cases.label: SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: DR-001 2.2 states application and system logs are retained for 90 days.

cases.claim: A vendor security review must be renewed every 12 months.
cases.label: SUPPORTED

cases.claim: Employees may carry over an unlimited number of unused PTO days.
cases.label: CONTRADICTED
cases.rationale: HR-001 2.3 caps carryover at 5 days; the rest is forfeited. 'Unlimited' contradicts this.

cases.claim: Passwords only need to be at least 8 characters.
cases.label: CONTRADICTED

cases.claim: Expense reports can be submitted up to 60 days after the expense.
cases.label: CONTRADICTED
cases.rationale: EXP-001 6.1 sets the deadline at 30 days.

cases.claim: Business class is automatically allowed on any flight over 6 hours.
cases.label: CONTRADICTED
cases.rationale: EXP-001 3.2 allows premium economy for 6+ hour flights; 3.3 requires VP approval for business class regardless of length, so it is not automatic.

cases.claim: Employees receive a $1,000 annual home-office stipend.
cases.label: NOT_IN_DOCS
cases.rationale: No document mentions a home-office stipend. Plausible benefit, but absent - must not be reported as supported.

cases.claim: Northwind Labs offers a 5% 401(k) matching contribution.
cases.label: NOT_IN_DOCS
cases.rationale: Retirement matching is not addressed anywhere in the corpus.

cases.claim: Employees are entitled to 5 days of bereavement leave.
cases.label: NOT_IN_DOCS
cases.rationale: The handbook defines PTO, sick leave, and parental leave only; bereavement leave is not mentioned.

cases.claim: Every vendor must provide a SOC 2 report before onboarding.
cases.label: NOT_IN_DOCS
cases.rationale: The vendor policy requires a security review and a DPA where applicable, but never mentions a SOC 2 report.

cases.claim: New hires get 18 PTO days per year and may carry all of them into the next year.
cases.label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: The 18-day figure is supported by 2.1, but 'carry all of them' contradicts the 5-day carryover cap in 2.3.

cases.claim: Client meals are reimbursable up to $150 per attendee, including unlimited alcohol.
cases.label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: The $150 per-attendee cap is supported by 4.2, but alcohol is capped at $50 per attendee, so 'unlimited alcohol' is false.

cases.claim: Restricted data must not be stored on personal devices, but it may be pasted into approved AI tools.
cases.label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: The personal-device prohibition is supported by 3.2, but 4.2 forbids pasting Confidential or Restricted data into third-party AI tools, contradicting the second clause.

cases.claim: A $12,000/year vendor handling Confidential data needs both a security review and VP plus Legal approval.
cases.label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
cases.rationale: A security review is required (2.2 by value and 3.1 by data type), but VP and Legal approval is only required at $50,000+/year (2.3), so it is not required at $12,000.
